description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of interactions between olfactory emotion induction and n-back working memory in schizophrenia patients and healthy volunteers using functional MRI.

value: Healthy subjects revealed significantly stronger brain activation in the anterior cingulate gyrus and the right superior frontal cortex during the interaction of working memory and negative emotion.
Increased activation in patients was observed in the left middle frontal and the medial part of the left orbitofrontal gyrus.

The decreased anterior cingulate and dorsomedial prefrontal activation in patients may indicate that patients fail to adjust to heightened demands, whereas increased orbitofrontal activation may result from insufficient suppression of emotional responses and greater irritation induced by the odour.
